subject: Sizing intake: concurrency & token landscape for Dedicated proposal (QortexAI)
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@qortex.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing intake: initial telemetry and a couple questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this on. Per our quick call, attaching a small telemetry extract from our production edge (7 days) — it has per-request token counts, request type (chat vs. completion), and a small sample of KV cache hit flags. We generally see a bimodal prompt length (small completions ~20 tokens and long context builds ~1200 tokens).

Couple of clarifying Qs before your sizing pass:
- How do you treat long-running chat sessions for KV cache occupancy? Do you assume sticky sessions to a GPU or pool-level affinity?
- Our traffic has a pronounced morning spike (07:00–10:00 PT) and smaller sustained tail. How do you advise sizing burst vs. steady-state capacity for a Dedicated pool?

Attaching: traffic_sample.csv (first 10k rows) and a heatmap export.

Olivia
Senior Engineering Manager
QortexAI

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@qortex.ai>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@qortex.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing intake: initial telemetry and a couple questions

Hi Olivia — thanks for the sample, this is helpful. Quick answers up front, then a short request list so we can produce a confident Dedicated sizing: 

Short answers:
- KV cache assumptions: our default Dedicated sizing assumes session affinity within a pool (sticky to a host within the pool) for conversational flows longer than ~200 tokens, which preserves KV efficiency. We will size for a conservative 60% effective KV reuse unless you provide explicit session stickiness targets.
- Burst vs steady-state: we recommend reserving capacity for 95th-percentile sustained throughput and planning a burst buffer (20–40% additional GPUs or autoscale headroom) to cover the morning spike depending on latency SLOs.

Things we need to finalize numbers (quick asks):
1) A 72-hour high-resolution sample (CSV/Parquet) including timestamp, request_type, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, kv_cache_hit (boolean), and latency_ms at p50/p95/p99 if available.
2) Clarify latency SLO for interactive chat (target p95 <= 300ms for short prompts? or are you OK with larger for long-context completions).
3) Expected session concurrency per user (avg/max) or a proxy (e.g., active sessions per minute).

If you prefer, I can draft a mutual action plan (MAP) with concrete deliverables and dates. Proposed internal timeline: we can turn around a first-pass sizing in 3 business days after receiving the 72-hour sample.

Exporting to a short MAP and sending to Karthik/Monica to help with GPU SKU and quantization suggestions.

Thanks — Neha
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@qortex.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing intake: initial telemetry and a couple questions

Looping in a couple of sizing heuristics I want us to consider for Qortex: 

Notes:
- Prompt/response length mix: with a bimodal distribution (20 tokens vs 1200 tokens), effective GPU occupancy is dominated by the long-context jobs. For cost-efficient Dedicated fleet planning, we should consider 2-class routing: keep short completions on lower-cost SKUs with higher oversubscription and route long-context sessions to a smaller pool of high-memory GPUs with KV cache affinity.
- KV cache: 60% reuse assumption is reasonable for first-pass, but please ask Olivia for session stickiness target — that can materially reduce required memory headroom.
- Burst sizing: instead of static headroom, propose an autoscale policy with a short warm-up window (60–90s) plus a reserved burst of 10% additional GPUs in the Dedicated quota to hit hard morning spikes without heavy overcommit.

I will prepare a quick tabular projection (GPU type mix, expected occupancy, cost/hr estimate) once we get the 72-hour sample.

—Karthik
Senior Pre-Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@qortex.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@qortex.ai>
Date: 2026-06-16T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing intake: initial telemetry and a couple questions

Thanks Neha and Karthik — answering inline:
- We can provide the 72-hour high-res export by EOD tomorrow (06/17). It will include timestamp, request_type (chat/completion), prompt_tokens, response_tokens, kv_cache_hit, and p50/p95/p99 latencies by request id.
- Latency SLO: target p95 <= 350ms for short interactive prompts (<=100 tokens). For long-context flows (>500 tokens) we're flexible to p95 <= 1s as long as p99 stays acceptable.
- Session stickiness: we can give a best-effort session affinity token; currently our edge LB is sticky for ~15 minutes but we can look into extending to 1h for prioritized customers.

Samir is copied to coordinate the telemetry export. Appreciate the MAP — that will make internal approvals clearer on our side.

Olivia

Hi Olivia / Samir — great, thanks. Attached is a short MAP and our assumptions summary. Key decision points for you to confirm:

1) Session affinity target: please confirm whether you can extend LB stickiness to >45 minutes for prioritized tenants (recommended) — this will reduce memory footprint and GPUs needed by ~15–25% in our model.
2) Latency SLO confirmation: p95 <= 350ms (<=100 token) and p95 <= 1s (>500 token) accepted?
3) Telemetry delivery: we expect the 72-hour export and the CSV sample by EOD 06/17 — once received we will run an occupancy simulation and return a sizing table (GPU SKUs, count, expected occupancy, and cost delta) in 3 business days.

Attached: mutual_action_plan.docx (MAP) with deadlines and a short assumptions table.

Next internal steps (Redwood): Karthik will run the occupancy/eviction model and Monica will produce an autoscaling + fallback policy recommendation. We'll include a conservative quantized model candidate to show unit-cost tradeoffs.

If that all looks good I will schedule a 30-min walkthrough with the Qortex infra team on Tuesday (06/22).

Thanks — Neha
